annotations.text:
Nine screens, one chrome, light only.

The old connector-auth screen and the action Auth tab had the same purpose — and the action one was worse than redundant: its whole content was "it is over there". That is the signpost tab I removed from the connector earlier in the session and then rebuilt one level down.

So: a connector is Name, Description, Tags and its Actions — identity and contents, nothing else. Base URL and auth moved onto the action Auth tab, where they are used, and are editable there.

A connector has no tabs and now barely has a screen: three identity rows and the Actions table.

Screen 2 is one with nothing in it — no empty-state message, no Add button. The last row of the table is the affordance, and Publish is greyed because a connector with no actions cannot usefully be published.

The founder's own API: 13 fields under one `detail` object.

day, month, year, lat and lon are required by the API and every one shows a dash — Meta records required-ness only for TOP-LEVEL body fields, and the only top-level field here is `detail`. So the description carries the range, the unit and the word required. There is no min, max or pattern either.

The response is 200 OK with status:failed. A green tick on the status line would report success on a failed call, so the pane shows the body and the strip says read status, not the code.

Still no Add button — the trailing row is the add, sitting where the new row appears.

What actually helps at nine or twenty params: Bulk swaps the table for one line per parameter, Tab off the last row makes the next one, and pasting a query string fills rows in one go. A button would add a click per row and nothing else.

Switching Table/Bulk loses nothing — same data, two ways to type it.

One tab row, ever, and it lives inside an action.

Response is pinned to the foot of the pane on EVERY action screen — a 44px "Not sent yet" strip until you Send, then 268px with the status line and the body. It does not move between tabs.

Every table is the same five columns: Key · Type · Source · Description · Required.

Auth, collapsed from two screens into one.

Editable, because this is where you are when you need it. Marked shared, because it is: Meta keeps base_url and auth_config on the connector and a tool cannot carry a credential of its own, so one edit changes every action under it.

The In column — Header / Query / Body — is the gap that stops an ?api_key= API being configurable at all today.

Import cURL is the highest-value screen here, and not for the obvious reason.

Every API doc ships a curl example, so pasting one is the fastest way in — method, base URL, path, headers and all 13 body fields in one action.

The real value is that it is the FIRST moment we can tell the truth. A curl with a form-encoded or multipart body means the API cannot be connected at all, and saying that on paste beats discovering it at publish. It can also spot an api_key sitting in the query string, a Basic auth flag we have no auth type for, and a signature header we cannot compute per request.

So the honesty gap (G7) is not a paragraph in the Body tab. It is a check that runs the moment someone brings us an API.
